The name Orleah carries the meaning “Mountain of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English. Parents who choose Orleah usually hope their child will grow to embody mountain of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: אורלה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אורלה הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'אור שלי' או 'אור אלוהים'. הוא מורכב משתי מילים: 'אור' שפירושו אור, ו'לה' שיכולה להיות קיצור של 'אל' או 'לאה'. השם אורלה מבטא את הקשר בין האור האלוהי לאדם.

in_greek.name: Ορλεά
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ορλεά είναι μια μορφή του ονόματος που σημαίνει 'Φως Θεού' ή 'Φως του Θεού'. Η ετυμολογία του ονόματος συνδέεται με τις λέξεις 'φως' και 'Θεός', εκφράζοντας τη σχέση μεταξύ του θείου φωτός και του ανθρώπου.

in_latin.name: Orleah
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Orleah significat 'Lux Dei' seu 'Lumen Dei'. Etymologia nominis coniungit verba 'lux' et 'Deus', exprimens relationem inter lucem divinam et hominem. Nomen Orleah in traditione christiana lucem et vitam afferre significat.

historical_references.reference: Orleana, the daughter of King Louis XII of France, was given the title 'Orleanna of Valois' or 'Orleah of Valois' after her birth in 1468. The name 'Orleah' comes from the Old French word 'Orleaan', which means 'of Orleans'. The region of Orleans was significant during the Hundred Years War between France and England, and the name served to remind the people of their connection to this important part of their history.

In the novel 'The Scarlet Letter' by Nathaniel Hawthorne, published in 1850, the protagonist Hester Prynne names her daughter 'Pearl', but in the community's records she is registered as 'Orleana'. This name is likely a reference to the French noblewoman 'Orleana of Valois', as Hester and her husband Chillingworth had spent some time in France before settling in the New World. The name 'Orleana' may have been chosen to signify Hester's connection to the powerful and noble French lineage.
